I will do it the way I usually farm, just with small adjustments. I have only 8.2 mu, so I cannot gamble. Wheat and maize feed the house and bring steady money, so I will keep most land in the wheat-maize rotation. Cotton takes more watching and more picking labor, and some people in my family work outside, so I will not plant too much cotton. I will put 6.2 mu into wheat, then after wheat harvest I will sow maize on that same 6.2 mu. The remaining 2.0 mu I will keep for cotton. I do mostly what worked before and what I see around me. If fertilizer is short, yield drops fast, and that loss hurts more than wasting a little fertilizer, so I will not cut too hard. With well water in hand, I will give wheat more water because wheat here cannot rely only on the sky. Maize I will water less but still give it key water when it needs it. Cotton I will keep smaller because it eats labor. I will use improved or hybrid seed where I have seen people nearby get a good stand and better harvest, but I will still farm in the old practical way: enough base fertilizer, clean field work, water on time, and spray when I see real pest pressure.
